# aos command index

Every public command, grouped, generated from the registry. This is the
complete list; `aos <group> <cmd> --help` has the full flag set, and
`aos commands` says what this particular machine can run right now.
Marks: *display* = needs a desktop session (exit 2 without one);
*blocking* = runs until stopped; *platforms* = only those OSes.

## adapters

Commands you add yourself, without writing a program

### `aos adapters list`

List the adapters this machine has loaded

```bash
aos adapters list [--json]
aos adapters list
```

### `aos adapters path`

Print the directory adapters are read from

```bash
aos adapters path
```

### `aos adapters example`

Print a starter adapter, ready to save and edit

```bash
aos adapters example [--write]
aos adapters example
aos adapters example --write
```


## audio

Output volume and mute

### `aos audio volume`

Print the output volume, or set it

```bash
aos audio volume [<0-100>|+<n>|-<n>]
aos audio volume
aos audio volume 40
aos audio volume +5
```

### `aos audio mute`

Print or change the output mute state

```bash
aos audio mute [on|off|toggle]
aos audio mute toggle
```


## battery

Battery presence and charge

### `aos battery status`

Print battery charge and charging state

```bash
aos battery status
```

### `aos battery present`

Exit 0 when a battery is present, 1 otherwise

```bash
aos battery present
aos battery present && echo has a battery
```

### `aos battery percent`

```bash

aos battery percent    # 87
```


## capture

Screenshots

### `aos capture screenshot`

Take a screenshot

*display · alias: screenshot*

```bash
aos capture screenshot [fullscreen|region|window] [--monitor=<n>] [--region=<x,y,w,h>] [--app=<name>] [--copy] [--out=<path>]
aos screenshot
aos capture screenshot region --copy
aos capture screenshot --monitor=2
aos capture screenshot --app=Chrome --out=/tmp/term.png
aos capture screenshot --region=0,0,800,600
```

### `aos capture video start`

Start recording the screen with ffmpeg (detached; ask the person first)

*display*

```bash
aos capture video start [smart|monitor|window|region|app|mouse] [--monitor=<n>] [--app=<name>|--title=<s>] [--region=<x,y,w,h>] [--fps=30] [--audio=none|mic|system|both] [--mic=<name|index>] [--zoom=2] [--out=<path.mp4>] [--max=10m] [--indicator=false] [--json]
aos capture video start smart --audio=mic --out=~/Movies/demo.mp4
aos capture video start monitor --monitor=2
aos capture video start mouse --zoom=2
aos capture video start app --app=Chrome
aos capture video start window --app=Terminal
aos capture video start region --region=0,0,1280,720 --max=2m
# exit 2 when ffmpeg (or a loopback device for --audio=system) is missing
```

### `aos capture video stop`

Stop recording, finalize the mp4 and render <out>.final.mp4 with the auto camera

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos capture video stop [--raw] [--json]
aos capture video stop
aos capture video stop --raw --json
```

### `aos capture video status`

Is a recording running, and where is it going

*display*

```bash
aos capture video status [--json]
aos capture video status
```

### `aos capture video mark`

Add a labelled event to the recording (a camera target with --rect)

*display*

```bash
aos capture video mark <label...> [--rect=<x,y,w,h>]
aos capture video mark "login works"
aos capture video mark "the chart" --rect=200,150,800,450
```

### `aos capture video focus`

Point the camera at a place until unfocus (or --hold)

*display*

```bash
aos capture video focus (--rect=<x,y,w,h> | --at=<x,y> [--size=640x360] | --app=<name>|--title=<s> [--find=<text> [--role=<r>]]) [--hold=<duration>] [--zoom=<factor>]
aos capture video focus --rect=100,100,800,450
aos capture video focus --at=640,400 --size=800x450 --hold=4s
aos capture video focus --app=Chrome --find="Sign in" --zoom=2
```

### `aos capture video unfocus`

Send the camera back to its automatic mode

*display*

```bash
aos capture video unfocus
```

### `aos capture video follow`

Switch the live camera: follow the mouse, an app, smart, or off

*display*

```bash
aos capture video follow mouse|app|smart|off [--app=<name>|--title=<s>]
aos capture video follow mouse
aos capture video follow app --app=Chrome
aos capture video follow off
```

### `aos capture video devices`

List the screens, microphones and system-audio sources ffmpeg can record

*display*

```bash
aos capture video devices [--json]
aos capture video devices
```

### `aos capture video zoom`

Re-render an aos recording with the auto camera, from its events file

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos capture video zoom <in.mp4> [--events=<file>] [--out=<file>] [--pad=0.15] [--max-zoom=2.5] [--ease=0.6] [--hold-wide=1.0] [--zoom=2] [--follow=mouse|app|smart|off] [--size=1920x1080] [--json]
aos capture video zoom ~/Movies/demo.mp4
aos capture video zoom demo.mp4 --max-zoom=2 --ease=0.8 --out=demo.cut.mp4
aos capture video zoom demo.mp4 --follow=off
```

## draw

Point at something on screen with a big arrow and a sign

### `aos draw`

Draw a click-through arrow + sign at a point, region, window, text or the mouse

*display*

```bash
aos draw (--at=<x,y> | --rect=<x,y,w,h> | <app> | --app=<name> | --title=<s> | --mouse) [--find=<text> [--role=<r>] [--source=<s>] [--exact] [--nth=<n>]] --text=<sign> [--style=arrow|ring|box] [--shape=bend|straight|zigzag|spiral] [--size=S|M|L] [--color=<name|#hex>] [--from=<side>] [--monitor=<n>] [--position=<side>] [--duration=<seconds>] [--detach] [--animate=on|off] [--preview=<out.png>] [--json]
aos draw --app=Calculator --find=7 --style=ring --text="press 7"
aos draw --at=640,400 --text="click here" --duration=5
aos draw --rect=100,100,400,200 --style=box --text="this area" --preview=/tmp/draw.png
aos draw --mouse --text="you are here" --detach
aos draw stop
# exit 3 when --find does not find the window or the text
```

### `aos draw text`

Show a styled text label (no arrow) inside a window, a monitor, a rect, or beside a point

*display*

```bash
aos draw text <text...> [--app=<name> | --title=<s> | --monitor=<n> | --rect=<x,y,w,h> | --at=<x,y> | --mouse] [--position=bottom-center|top-center|center|left|right|top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right] [--margin=<px|N%>] [--offset=<dx,dy>] [--color=<text colour>] [--bg=auto|none|<colour>] [--font=<name>] [--font-scale=<k>] [--size=S|M|L|XL] [--weight=regular|bold] [--align=left|center|right] [--max-width=<px|N%>] [--duration=<seconds>] [--detach] [--preview=<out.png>] [--json]
aos draw text "Step 2: pick a file" --app=Finder --position=top --color=amber
aos draw text "Done ✓" --monitor=2 --position=center --size=XL --color=green
aos draw text "Line one\nLine two" --rect=100,100,800,500 --position=bottom-right --bg=none
# default: bottom-center of the focused monitor (the recording's monitor while `capture video` runs), subtitle safe area (8% bottom, 5% sides)
```

### `aos draw stop`

Remove every detached drawing

*display*

```bash
aos draw stop [--json]
aos draw stop
```

### `aos draw config`

Show the draw defaults file, or create it with --init

*display*

```bash
aos draw config [--init] [--force]
aos draw config
aos draw config --init
```

### `aos draw fonts`

List the font names --font accepts

*display*

```bash

```


## exec

Run commands, with output streamed or captured

### `aos exec run`

Run a command with its output streamed to this terminal

```bash
aos exec run <command> [args...]
aos exec run git status
```

### `aos exec capture`

Run a command and print stdout, stderr, and exit code as JSON

```bash
aos exec capture <command> [args...]
aos exec capture git status
aos exec capture -- ls -la
```

### `aos exec shell`

Run a command line through the platform shell

```bash
aos exec shell <script>
aos exec shell "git log --oneline | head -5"
```


## file

Read, write, and inspect files

### `aos file read`

Print a file, optionally a line range

```bash
aos file read <path> [--lines=<from>:<to>]
aos file read go.mod
aos file read main.go --lines=10:40
```

### `aos file write`

Write stdin, or the given words, to a file

```bash
aos file write <path> [text...]
aos file write notes.txt "first line"
cat in.txt | aos file write out.txt
```

### `aos file append`

Append stdin, or the given words, to a file

```bash
aos file append <path> [text...]
aos file append log.txt "done"
```

### `aos file list`

List a directory

```bash
aos file list [path] [--all] [--json]
aos file list
aos file list ~/Downloads --json
```

### `aos file stat`

Print one path's size, mode, and modified time

```bash
aos file stat <path> [--json]
aos file stat go.mod --json
```

### `aos file mkdir`

Create a directory, including parents

```bash
aos file mkdir <path>
aos file mkdir ~/.config/aos/layouts
```

### `aos file copy`

Copy a file

```bash
aos file copy <source> <destination>
aos file copy a.txt b.txt
```

### `aos file move`

Move or rename a path

```bash
aos file move <source> <destination>
aos file move old.txt new.txt
```

### `aos file delete`

Delete a file, or a directory with --recursive

```bash
aos file delete <path> [--recursive]
aos file delete /tmp/scratch --recursive
```

## key

Keystrokes and typed text

### `aos key type`

Type text; with --app/--title it goes to that window without needing focus

*display*

```bash
aos key type <text...> [--app=<name>|--title=<substring> [--verify] [--focus] [--json]]
aos key type "hello world"
aos key type "hello" --app=TextEdit --verify   # posted to the app, read back from its text field
aos key type "hello" --app=Chrome --focus      # real focus + verify, focus handed back after
# exit 1 if --verify cannot see the text arrive; exit 3 if no window matches
```

### `aos key press`

Press a key combination

*display*

```bash
aos key press <combo> [--app=<name>|--title=<substring> [--focus] [--json]]
aos key press cmd+shift+s
aos key press enter --app=TextEdit   # posted to the app, no focus change
```

## obs

What this machine has been asked to do

### `aos obs stats`

Summarise recorded work: calls, failures, and latency per route

```bash

aos obs stats

```

### `aos obs tail`

Print the most recent spans, newest last

```bash
aos obs tail [--limit=<n>] [--since=<duration>]
aos obs tail --limit=20
```

### `aos obs export`

Emit recorded spans as OTLP JSON, ready for a collector

```bash
aos obs export [--since=<duration>]

```

### `aos obs audit`

Every command this machine was asked to run, oldest first

```bash
aos obs audit [--since=<duration>] [--source=<cli|mcp>] [--failed] [--json]
aos obs audit --since=24h
aos obs audit --source=mcp     # only what agents asked for
aos obs audit --failed
```

### `aos obs summary`

How much this machine is actually used, and by what

```bash
aos obs summary [--since=<duration>] [--json]
aos obs summary
aos obs summary --since=7d
```

### `aos obs path`

Print where telemetry is written

```bash

```

## serve

### `aos serve mcp`

Serve every command as an MCP tool over streamable HTTP

```bash

aos serve mcp --socket=~/.aos/serve.sock   # the host end of an SSH RemoteForward
aos serve mcp --addr=127.0.0.1:9000 --groups=window,capture,exec

```

### `aos serve tools`

Print the MCP tool catalogue this machine would expose


## tab

Browser and terminal tabs: list, focus, open, send, close

### `aos tab list`

List the tabs of every browser and terminal window

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*


### `aos tab focus`

Raise a tab's window and select the tab

```bash
aos tab focus (--title=<substring> | --url=<substring> | --cwd=<substring> | --id=<tab id>) [--app=<name>] [--kind=<kind>] [--exact]

aos tab focus --title=Inbox --app=Chrome

# exit 3 when no tab matches
```

### `aos tab open`


### `aos tab send`

Type text or press a key in a terminal tab without focusing it

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab send --id=<tab id> (--text=<text> | --key=<combo>)
aos tab send --id=ghostty:tab-group-8039faee0:tab-802a71200 --text="ls -la"
aos tab send --id=ghostty:tab-group-8039faee0:tab-802a71200 --key=enter
aos tab send --id=iterm:31:1 --key=ctrl+c
```

### `aos tab close`

Close one tab (never the whole window)

*display · platforms: darwin, windows*

```bash
aos tab close (--id=<tab id> | --title=<substring> | --url=<substring>) [--app=<name>] [--kind=<kind>] [--exact]
aos tab close --id=chrome:1658108662:1658109078
aos tab close --title=example --app=Chrome
```


## version

Version information

### `aos version`

Print the aos version

```bash
aos version
```


## watch

Follow what changes on this machine, one JSON line per event

### `aos watch clipboard`

Print a JSON line whenever the clipboard text changes

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch clipboard [--interval=<500ms>] [--max=<n>] [--content]
aos watch clipboard
aos watch clipboard --max=1 --content
```

### `aos watch window`

Print a JSON line whenever the focused window changes

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch window [--interval=<500ms>] [--max=<n>]
aos watch window
aos watch window --max=1
```

### `aos watch file`

Print a JSON line whenever a file or directory entry changes

*display · blocking*

```bash
aos watch file <path> [--interval=<500ms>] [--max=<n>] [--recursive]
aos watch file ~/Downloads
aos watch file ./notes.md --max=1
aos watch file ./src --recursive --interval=1s
```


## webapp

Open a site as a standalone browser window

### `aos webapp open`

Open a URL in a chromeless app window

*display*

```bash
aos webapp open <url>
aos webapp open https://app.slack.com
```


## window

Desktop windows: list, focus, move, resize, arrange

### `aos window list`

List open windows

*display*

```bash
aos window list [--app=<name>] [--title=<substring>] [--kind=browser|terminal|editor|files|other] [--json]
aos window list
aos window list --app=Chrome
aos window list --kind=terminal
```

### `aos window focus`

Bring a window to the front

*display*

```bash
aos window focus <app> | --app=<name> | --title=<substring>
aos window focus Chrome
```

### `aos window move`

Move a window to a zone, a split, or absolute bounds

*display*

```bash
aos window move <app> (--zone=<1A|2:1> | --at=<x,y,w,h>) [--monitor=<n>]
aos window move Chrome --zone=1B
aos window move Chrome --monitor=2 --zone=1:3
aos window move Slack --at=0,25,1920,1055
```

### `aos window resize`

Resize a window in place

*display*

```bash
aos window resize <app> --w=<width> --h=<height>
aos window resize Chrome --w=900 --h=700
```

### `aos window wait`

Wait for a window to appear, then print it

*display*

```bash
aos window wait <app> [--timeout=<ms>]
aos window wait Chrome --timeout=5000
```

### `aos window zones`

Show what each zone means on a real monitor

*display*

```bash
aos window zones [--monitor=<n>] [--show]
aos window zones
aos window zones --monitor=2
aos window zones --show --app=Chrome
```

### `aos window arrange`

Apply a saved layout of many windows in one pass

*display*

```bash
aos window arrange <layout.json | ->
aos window arrange ~/.config/aos/layouts/work.json
echo '[{"app":"Google Chrome","zone":"1A"},{"app":"Slack","zone":"1B"}]' | aos window arrange -
```

### `aos window save`

Save the current layout to a file `window arrange` can apply

*display*

```bash
aos window save <layout.json> [--app=<name>] [--monitor=<n>]
aos window save ~/.config/aos/layouts/work.json
aos window save ~/work.json --app=Chrome
aos window save ~/second-screen.json --monitor=2
```
